title: Luanda protest over diesel-price increase during taxi strike
threshold_50_evidence: Not established. Reuters reports protests in the capital but gives no crowd count or evidence that 50 or more people assembled at one place and time.

start_date.summary: Reuters dateline says Luanda, July 28; article published July 29.

location.summary: Reuters locates the reported protests in Luanda.

scope.summary: Reported in the capital; no other location is attached to this candidate.

demands.summary: Reuters describes protests over a diesel-price increase; it contextualizes the price change as a government subsidy-reduction policy.

state_response.summary: Reuters says police acknowledged arrests; it attributes tear gas, shots fired into the air, and fatality claims to Novo Jornal. Arrest count and physical crowd dispersal are not stated; deaths are not coded as state killings.

notes: A verified Reuters page reports protests over a diesel-price increase in Luanda on Monday, July 28, while a three-day minibus-taxi strike began that day. Keep the strike and public protest related but distinct; looting is not automatically coded as protester violence. Reuters attributes its death and police-force details to Novo Jornal. Attendance and meeting boundaries remain unknown.
open_questions: Was there a qualifying gathering of at least 50 people, and what exact time/place bounds can be supported?
Can the Novo Jornal origin reporting be located and accessed under its own exact-URL publisher/story scope review, or should attributed claims remain the limit?
Were arrests tied to protesters at this specific assembly, and was any assembled crowd physically dispersed?
Did the protest assembly continue, end, or recur after July 28?
